New study shows dogs understand human vocal tones.

What's their next study?

"New study shows dogs understand words"

Probably something more obvious.

"New study finds most cats don't like people."
This is very unsurprising. Many animals can understand human vocal tones, not to mention other animal's vocal tones. There are universal sounds that animals can interpret to various degrees.

And vice versa is true. Humans can easily tell if a dog is angry, scared, excited, happy, etc based on how it barks. It seems common sense, but when you really think about it it's remarkable. There's no other animal we can do that with (besides cats in some more basic ways because they mimic human baby sounds). It's why humans and dogs have been natural companions for millennia, from hunting to the battlefield to farming to just companionship, we've always found dogs to be our closest interspecies friend.

Hell, dogs don't even need vocal tones to discern moods.

One of my dogs can tell when I'm playing the harmonica for fun or for practice. She sings along when it's just for fun, but only watches when I'm working on a new lick. She also knows based on how I handle a guitar whether she's allowed to jump/frolic near me. At this point I'm pretty sure she recognizes the Taylor logo and just knows to go lay down when she sees one.

Their level of comprehension is far higher than many humans. Every ding on my instruments came from some stupid adult human or another.

Poor dog in the test looked like "what did I do to deserve this?!?"

Anyway, this study is probably fairly obvious to most people. What isn't obvious to most people is what else dogs can understand about humans. They use our vocal tones and sounds to determine what we're trying to say, of course, but they also use our body language to figure us out as well. Dogs can also sense whether or not someone is afraid of them or confident around them, and they read a lot into that factor alone. If a dog thinks you're afraid of it, then it is immediately suspicious of you. This might make the dog think that you will attack it out of fear (that's a pretty common response for any animal) and so it might fight back, or a dog might see you as an inferior rank in whatever social setting. Conversely, if you are confident around a dog, they will probably assume you're doing what you're supposed to be doing and are no threat to them, or they might assume that you are in a dominant social position, so they should show you due respect. Being confident around a dog puts them at ease because they know they can just follow your lead. Being afraid makes them worry that something about the situation is not right, which puts them on edge.

They use the same part of the brain to process it.
